trigger: Breach of security (unauthorized access to electronic personal information) of Florida residents. Here: guarantor and applicant names with Social Security numbers or driver license numbers (leasing folder, email); employee Social Security numbers in HR files. Badge holder names, employers, and credential numbers are not listed elements. Whether door access history is 'information regarding an individual's geolocation' (501.171(1)(g)1.a.(VII)) and whether face match templates are 'biometric data as defined in s. 501.702' (item (VI)) are open questions for counsel; the company plans as if both were covered
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. Clock starts at the determination, not at discovery; record the date. A 15-day extension is available only for this notice, on written good cause given to the department within the 30 days (501.171(3)(a))
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email; the notice gives the date or date range, the data involved, and a contact (501.171(4)(e)). Substitute notice only in the cases in 501.171(4)(f)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes, if the leasing folder, email, or HR files were accessed (about 60 guarantors and applicants, 7 employees). Ransomware limited to the BAS workstation (setpoints, schedules, graphics) is not personal information

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after the determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (no extension for this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General), with the content listed in 501.171(3)(b)
applies_at_this_tier: Not expected: even counting every credential holder's door history, the company holds personal information on fewer than 500 people. Recount in every incident

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (as defined in 15 U.S.C. 1681a(p)): timing, distribution, and content of the notices
applies_at_this_tier: No under current counts (well under 1,000 people)

trigger: After an appropriate investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or other financial harm
deadline: Written determination kept at least 5 years and provided to the department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only if counsel supports it; not likely when Social Security numbers were taken

trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that individual notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period in the agency's written request; the agency may extend or revoke in writing
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains, stores, or processes personal information for the company (property management system, payroll service, tenant screening service, access control platform, cloud backup through the MSP) has a breach
deadline: The vendor must notify the company as expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after its determination; the company then owes the 501.171(3) and (4) notices
applies_at_this_tier: Yes. The security addendum asks vendors for 24 hours (POL-02 A.5)

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Affected individuals (guarantors, applicants, employees, credential holders) who reside outside Florida
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Residents, and the state attorney general or regulator where that state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Check the residence of every affected individual; some guarantors of tenant businesses live in other states

citation: Leases signed since 2024 (security incident clause); all leases (building service interruption notices)
trigger: Unauthorized access to tenant employees' data in the access control system; or building services (HVAC, access) degraded
deadline: Leases since 2024: within 72 hours of learning of unauthorized access (counsel to confirm when each clause's clock starts; plan from discovery). Service interruptions: the same business day
notify: Each tenant's designated contact, by the lease notice method (printed contact list in the binder)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal. Notify tenants on older leases at the same time

citation: Merchant agreement; PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.10.1 (SAQ P2PE) incident response plan
trigger: Suspected compromise of card data or tampering with the P2PE terminal
deadline: Per the merchant agreement and the P2PE Instruction Manual (Bookkeeper to confirm the time in the agreement)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if card data or the terminal is involved. BAS ransomware does not reach the stand-alone cellular terminal

trigger: Suspected security incident, extortion demand, or data theft
deadline: Per policy: prompt notice through the 24x7 breach hotline, before hiring outside firms; use panel counsel and forensics

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: All U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI
citation: CISA CPG 2.0 goal 5.B (voluntary); no statute requires it for this company
trigger: Ransomware or other significant cyber incident
deadline: As soon as practical; the runbook targets within 24 hours of declaration and before any ransom decision
notify: CISA (incident reporting on cisa.gov) and the FBI field office or IC3
applies_at_this_tier: Voluntary. Recommended: it supports OFAC mitigation and may bring technical help

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity
deadline: Statute: 72 hours after reasonable belief of a covered incident; 24 hours after a ransom payment. Not in effect until the final rule is effective
applies_at_this_tier: No. Final rule not published as of 2026-09-25, and the company would not be covered under the NPRM's criteria (size; P03). Recheck when the final rule is published

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after the materiality determination
applies_at_this_tier: No. The company is privately held

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or Kaspersky covered article report
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or services, or a Kaspersky covered article, in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases
applies_at_this_tier: No. The company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts (confirmed by the Managing Member). Recheck if that changes, because the cameras have not been screened for covered brands
